prerequisites: It is advisable to have passed courses related to Strength of Materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the characteristics, properties and behavior of structural steel and structural steel products.
Understand the general principles for the analysis and design of structural steel structures.
Show common structural typologies in metal structure buildings, particularly industrial constructions, as well as their elements and structural connections.
Size and check metal structural elements subjected to tension, compression, torsion, and bending forces.
Size and check welded and bolted metal structural connections.
Know the procedures for execution, assembly, and protection of metal structures.

syllabus_topics: Structural steel and structural steel products
Calculation bases, design regulations and frequent typologies of metal building structures
Actions (regulations) and solicitations (analysis models) in building structures
Particular calculation bases for metal building structures
Structural configuration of industrial constructions. Preliminary structural analysis.
Analysis and dimensioning of metallic structural elements
Uniform, warping and mixed torsion of thin-walled sections
Buckling of ideal and real compressed members
Elastic and plastic analysis of tensioned and flexed members
Instability phenomena in flexed members (lateral buckling and panel buckling)
Frequent typologies and global behavior of connections
Local analysis, dimensioning and execution of bolted connections
Local analysis, dimensioning and execution of welded connections
teaching_methods: Completion of assignments and evaluation tests

assessment_methods.method: Written test on the theory of the first part of the course
Written test on the problems of the first part of the course
Written test on the theory of the second part of the course
Written test on the problems of the second part or voluntary practical course work

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in each of the four evaluation procedures, and an average grade of 5 or higher. Students who do not meet these minimums must retake the deficient parts in the second call. For exchange students, the evaluation system may be modified if academic calendars do not coincide. An exceptional evaluation system consists of a theoretical test (40%) and two problem tests (20% and 40%), each also requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10.
